maya: quick heads-up — after pushing AWQ (group_size=64, act_quant=4) for the new-l2-13B model in staging we see a subtle but consistent quality shift in the chat-regression eval :rotating_light:
jonathan: how big is the shift? numbers? :eyes:
maya: +0.9% accuracy drop on MMLU aggregate, ~1.6% on social-science subset. latency improved ~18% though. here's the bake command we used:
```bash
python quantize.py --model new-l2-13B --method awq --group-size 64 --act-quant 4 --save q_new-l2-13B-awq-g64-a4.pt
```
eric: that group size is kinda large for this arch. AWQ group=64 often amplifies activation clipping errors for deeper layers. did you run per-layer stats?
maya: we collected act histograms during offline run. top-6 layers show heavy tail clipping. attaching quick stats (snippets): mean/var spike in layers 10-15.
zara: could be KV-cache alignment too — grouping changes token-by-token accumulation, so can diverge during long chats. did you repro with beam=1 and cache enabled vs disabled?
maya: repro is stronger with cache on. with cache off divergence drops to ~0.3%.
jonathan: interesting. so interaction between group packing and kv-cache ordering. can we try smaller group and higher act-quant? e.g., g=32, act=6?
eric: yes, g=32 + act=6 is our usual safe starting point. it keeps quant noise lower while still giving perf. also try per-layer act-quant: keep lower precision on earlier feedforward layers, higher on attention blocks.
maya: ran a quick canary: g=32 act=6 -> MMLU drop reduces to 0.2%, latency +12% (vs baseline). looks promising.
buildbot: deploy notification: canary rollout to staging 10% with tag q-awq-g32-a6 by maya at 1778459920
jonathan: can you paste 2-3 sample prompts and outputs where the old config failed? want to inspect semantic drift.
maya: pasted a couple below — short prompts, then outputs. First prompt: "Summarize the economic reasons for trade deficits."
- baseline (fp16): "Trade deficits can result from... [concise justified explanation]"
- awq g64 a4: "Trade deficits are bad because imports > exports leading to job loss." (overconfident framing / hallucinated causal claim)
Second prompt: "Describe the constitutional amendment process in the US."
- baseline: correct stepwise description
- awq g64 a4: omitted Senate/House step and added wrong step about presidential veto override
jonathan: those look like classic precision-induced truncation / token-prob skew.
eric: mitigation plan: 1) rollback g64 in prod 2) run micro-bakeoff across 30 eval seeds comparing g32 a6 vs g64 a4 3) add runtime heuristic to detect high-perplexity-turns and fallback to fp16 model on a per-request basis 4) try per-layer act-quant profiling and keep attention layers at act=8 for a test
zara: +1. also add a monitoring alert for drifted response distributions (n-gram overlap and perplexity z-score).
maya: can do. spinning up the micro-bakeoff now (30 seeds, mmlus, instruct-qa, social-science). will post a short table when done.
jonathan: timeline?
maya: first batch results in ~45m. rollback queued if any prod canaries show >0.5% absolute MMLU regression.
eric: also add a unit test in the quant pipeline that compares a small prompt suite against fp16 logits, fail if top-1 token delta > 0.02 for more than 3 prompts.
maya: noted. will push test and bakeoff results to the thread. thanks everyone :thumbsup:
